newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai listed firm 1996 results improved-paper.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai listed firm 1996 results improved-paper.

text.p: The annual results of Shanghai-listed firms were much better in 1996 than in 1995, based on the per-share earnings of 46 companies issuing annual reports, the Shanghai Securities News said on Wednesday. The 1996 earnings of the 46 firms averaged 0.4977 yuan per share, up from 0.27 yuan in 1995, it said.
A key factor behind the rise was China's improved national economy which led to cuts in bank interest rates last May and August, the newspaper said.
Management of listed companies also improved, it said.
Many listed Chinese firms posted poor results in 1994 and 1995, in part, because poor management left them unable to cope with austerity measures introduced in 1993.
All listed firms are required to post the previous year's annual results by April 30.
China has 566 listed firms, with 303 in Shanghai and 263 in Shenzhen.
To date, only 21 firms, all of them listed on the Shenzhen exchange, have reported their 1996 results.
